subject: Ronin Health: subprocessor custody and CAIQ evidence transfer
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@roninhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor roster + CAIQ extract request

Hi Irene / team,

We're kicking off a quick compliance window as part of Ronin Health's vendor intake for an upcoming pilot. Can you please provide the following by EOD May 18: 1) up-to-date subprocessor roster (CSV) with region/residency columns, 2) a compact CAIQ answers PDF, and 3) a SIG extract or mapping for the services used by our tenant.

Two clarifications that matter for our privacy review: does any subprocessor have access to unencrypted customer content or PII? If so, who and for what purpose? Also please confirm KMS/residency — we need to know where key material is held for our account and whether you support onshore key residency for US and EU customers.

Finally, what secure transfer options do you offer for evidence bundles? We prefer SFTP or an encrypted Drive share and a separate password channel.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Director, Compliance Programs
Ronin Health

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@roninhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + CAIQ extract request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver all three artifacts and a short cover note that maps the SIG domains to the Redwood services your tenant uses. High-level answers below and we'll attach the bundle by EOD Tuesday (May 12):

- Subprocessor access: No subprocessor processes or stores customer plaintext content for production inference. Logs/telemetry are limited and pseudonymized for ops; access is role-based and audited.
- KMS/residency: For hosted customers we use tenant-scoped envelope keys. Primary key material for US tenants is resident in us-east-1 HSMs; for EU tenants we offer eu-west-1 residency on request.
- Transfer options: we can push the bundle to a pre-shared S3 presigned URL, an SFTP endpoint, or a shared Drive folder with link + separate password. Let us know which you prefer.

I copied Jonas and Marissa to handle the artifact packaging and the SIG mapping. Two quick Qs for scope: do you need the full SOC 2 report or just the SOC 2 cover letter and the relevant control excerpts? Also, which tenant(s) should we scope the KMS residency statements to (pilot-ronin-prod or pilot-ronin-staging)?

Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@roninhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + CAIQ extract request

Alex — attaching the export and compact artifacts per Irene's plan. Bundle details below; password for the zip will be sent via SMS to the cell number on file (or we can use a short-lived DocuSign protected link if you prefer).

Attachments (included in zip):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260512.csv (columns: vendor_name, service, purpose, data_type_processed, region, access_level, contact)
- CAIQ-compact-answers-2026.pdf (compact Q&A focused on inference, telemetry, and key management)
- SIG-extract-2026.zip (SIG rows filtered to domains in use by Ronin Health)

Quick answers pulled from the roster:
- "TelemetryOps, Inc." is listed for monitoring and aggregated metrics; they receive pseudonymized request-level telemetry only and never process persisted customer content unencrypted.
- Encryption: all customer payloads are envelope-encrypted and stored encrypted at rest. For Ronin Health's pilot we can set primary key residency to us-east-1 (default) or enable eu-west-1 on request with an addendum. Keys are backed by HSM-managed KMS.
- SOC 2: we provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts (control mappings) for vendor reviews; full reports require an NDA/secure transfer. If you need the full report please confirm and we'll arrange a secure delivery channel.

Delivery options: we uploaded the bundle to a restricted Drive folder (link below) and can also push to your SFTP endpoint if you provide creds. Please confirm the destination and whether you want the full SOC 2 report.

--- Forwarded message ---
On May 10, 2026, at 09:12, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@roninhealth.com> wrote:

Marissa Cole
Compliance Programs Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@roninhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@roninhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + CAIQ extract request

Marissa/Irene — received the bundle, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) TelemetryOps: the roster shows their role as "metrics and alerting". Can you confirm whether the telemetry includes request/response traces (even if pseudonymized) or only aggregated/rollup metrics? Our security team flags any vendor that may retain traces with timestamps.
2) SOC 2: we only need the SOC 2 Type II control excerpts for now; if we decide we need the full report we'll request an NDA and a secure transfer.

Also, we couldn't open SIG-extract-2026.zip yet because it's password protected. Please send the password via the secure channel you mentioned. Once we validate the entries we'll confirm closure of this intake.

Thanks — Alex
